messages.subject: GC object allocation syntax
messages.body_plain:
I'm thinking I'd like to change the syntax that CXXR uses to allocate GC objects.

Currently allocation looks like:
   RObject *p = CXXR_NEW(RObject);
or
   RObject *p = new RObject;
   p->expose;

I'd like to change this use a factory method:
    RObject *p = RObject::New();

Doing this has a few advantages:
   - The exposure logic can be pushed into the factory method, simplifying things.
   - It would allow smarter allocation methods.  Vectors could have their elements allocated directly after the object (as CR does) etc.
   - The exposure mechanism could be replaced with a single GCInhibitor in the factory method, which is easier to understand and less error-prone.

Is there any good reason not to do this?

As far as I can tell, there are only a couple of places in the code where this might cause semantic differences to the code: saveload.cpp line 351 and Frame.cpp line 59, but according to my understanding of the code, both of those should be safe (or could use a GCInhibitor otherwise).

Thanks

messages.subject: Re: GC object allocation syntax
messages.body_plain:
Yes.  In terms of the public class interface, it's just replacing the regular constructor with the factory method.

Looking at the code, my guess is that the current arrangement is largely historical, as exposure used to be handled on a per-object basis, instead of simply disabling gc altogether.  Under that scheme, this approach wouldn't work.

messages.subject: Re: GC object allocation syntax
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrew,

The particular case that I have in mind is actually frames.  I'm looking into creating a frame class that contains space both for promises and a moderate number of bindings, all in the same contiguous memory block.  Using such a type should significantly reduce function call overhead (both fewer memory allocations and better cache locality) and result in fewer GC objects that need to be cleaned up after function calls.  Using factory New would allow the space for promises (and maybe bindings) to be sized correctly for each function call.

The extension of this to other types is IMHO mostly cleanup.  It'd presumably have some performance impact on short vectors, but not scalars since CXXR already handles those efficiently.  When I have some time (and I don't think it's high priority), I'll put together a CL, so we can discuss this with all the details.

Karl
